bridge_assessment.input_semantics_and_units: Still require the upstream contract; do not assume angle, angle-rate, torque, curvature, target speed, or acceleration are interchangeable.
bridge_assessment.longitudinal: With current scale=1/offset=0 and unfiltered_input=true, valid acceleration in m/s^2 is copied into both SCC acceleration-request fields, quantized to 0.01 m/s^2, without host jerk slew. standstill_analysis.source: Current src/command_adapter.cpp, safety_supervisor.cpp and active YAML; pinned opendbc Hyundai CAN-FD steering limits and DBC.
standstill_analysis.host_permission: The current lateral path has no minimum-moving-speed requirement; stationary takeover and normal lateral/Panda permission are still required.
standstill_analysis.feedback_path_at_zero_speed: low_speed_factor_v[0]=15 produces nonzero proportional error through factor squared. Desired/actual lateral acceleration and acceleration-based friction/feedforward are zero at v=0. Integral accumulation freezes below 5 m/s by default, so increasing friction or ki alone does not add standstill torque in the current formula.
standstill_analysis.tuning_scope: Increasing low-speed proportional weighting or kp can increase a below-cap torque request; it cannot increase the final +/-270-count ceiling. Steering ratio is a model parameter; slew changes the rise time, not the ceiling.
standstill_analysis.direct_torque_path: An upstream torque controller should supply Panda counts in direct_torque mode; local ratio/PID/friction/low-speed generation is bypassed, while existing count/slew/driver/engagement gates remain. Current default YAML remains steering_rate_deg_s.
standstill_analysis.vehicle_capability: No stronger standstill steering guarantee or supported native parking/angle interface established for this MDPS. Software saturation does not establish ECU acceptance or physical output.
standstill_analysis.actions: Explanation and persistent-state record only. No parameter/controller/firmware change, tests, CAN transmission, Panda queries or ECU diagnostics.

force_assessment.native_alternatives: PA/RSPA and ACI are interfaces to investigate, not verified stronger-force methods on this vehicle; an angle interface alone does not guarantee more torque.

parking_interface_research.pinned_dbc_evidence: MDPS 0xEA defines MDPS_PaPlugInSta, MDPS_PaModeSta, MDPS_PaCanfltSta and MDPS_PaStrAnglVal. Its generic PA mode enumeration includes ready/waiting for a PA command, standby and two activation steps. These are status/feedback definitions, not proof of support or a complete command protocol for this vehicle.
parking_interface_research.spas_scope: Pinned DBC defines SPAS1 0x165 with unidentified NEW_SIGNAL fields and SPAS2 0x16A with BLINKER_CONTROL. Inspected Carrotpilot create_spas_messages sends an empty SPAS1 payload and blinker control in SPAS2; it does not implement parking target-angle steering.
parking_interface_research.aci_distinction: ADAS ACI/LFA_ALT native angle control in the researched fork is separate from PA parking cooperation. Its existence does not establish either interface on this 2022 HDA1 MDPS.
parking_interface_research.current_repository: Current codec and selected ECAN-only Panda profile implement LFA torque steering; a usable PA command path is not implemented. Existing MDPS reception does not establish that PA commands reach the MDPS on the same bus. A configuration-only switch is insufficient.
parking_interface_research.feasibility: Conditional and unresolved. RSPA absence neither proves latent PA support nor proves that the MDPS hardware/firmware cannot support it. Required missing evidence: exact MDPS hardware/software and PA capability, command/activation/timeout protocol, and vehicle CAN routing. No separate connector, coding-only enable, ECU replacement requirement, or higher torque authority is established.
parking_interface_research.actions: Source research and documentation/state updates only. No builds, implementation tests, Panda USB access, CAN transmission, ECU diagnostics, firmware flash, wiring change or runtime/configuration change.

ecu_recovery.scope: Recover communication and restore stock camera/radar ownership while retaining output shutdown during an outage; does not automatically resume actuator output or reset an ECU during driving.
root_causes_fixed: Failed enter_no_output_mode cleanup had no persistent retry path
restore_ecu cleared disabled state before confirming resumed stock traffic
An armed failure could leave the automatic-arm path enabled
ecu_recovery.retry_policy: First cleanup is immediate; failed attempts wait 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then at most 30 seconds. Retrying continues while the process is running; disconnected Panda waits for the existing USB reconnect loop.
ecu_recovery.restoration: Restore radar then camera; on retry first observe valid stock CAN traffic to tolerate a lost acknowledgement, otherwise re-enter the diagnostic session and restore communication. Retain pending flags until stock traffic returns. Verify Panda NO_OUTPUT/mode/param/controls state before reporting completion.
ecu_recovery.stock_frame_validation: Only correct-size, checksum-valid 0x12A/0x1A0 received frames confirm stock traffic; returned/rejected frames do not count.
ecu_recovery.output_and_rearm: Hard faults and expired temporary-steering windows still stop all actuator output, inhibit automatic rearm, and use the existing pending stock-ECU restoration path. Pending restoration rejects rearm. Explicit acknowledgement/rearm and stationary physical activation conditions remain. A temporary EPS pause keeps the existing ECU ownership and may resume within its separate 3-second window.
ecu_recovery.observed_vehicle_recovery: Not tested. Communication restoration cannot guarantee recovery from ECU hardware faults or a physically broken CAN/USB path.
ecu_recovery.hardware_actions: None: no CAN transmission, USB control writes, ECU diagnostic requests, or firmware flash executed in this request.

carrotpilot_comparison.scope: Read-only source research of the current default branch snapshot; no runtime-pin, control-code, firmware, or vehicle changes.
model_to_can: modeld publishes modelV2.action desiredCurvature, desiredAcceleration, desiredVelocity, and shouldStop; targets may be derived from the predicted plan or a model action head.
Lateral path selects model action or lane-based lateralPlan, applies smoothing/curvature limiting, and uses a feedback controller to compute torque or angle according to vehicle configuration.
Longitudinal planner combines model trajectory/action, radar and cruise/MPC targets. ACC mode uses MPC; the other path takes the lower model/MPC acceleration and velocity targets.
LongControl combines target feedforward with measured speed or acceleration feedback, stop/start states and acceleration limits; controlsd publishes carControl at 100 Hz.

card calls CarInterface.apply, Hyundai CarController applies platform-specific conversion and limits, and the CAN packer constructs frames. sendcan passes through native pandad to Panda and vehicle CAN.
CAN-FD torque steering uses LFA TORQUE_REQUEST (the corresponding local pinned DBC signal is StrTqReqVal); SCC_CONTROL carries aReqRaw and aReqValue, with additional jerk shaping of aReqValue.
carrotpilot_comparison.feedback: carOutput.actuatorsOutput reports software CarController outputs. The requested-versus-returned steering comparison detects controller limiting; it is not ECU acknowledgement or physical torque measurement. CAN-FD CarState separately decodes MDPS steering/output torque and fault bits.
carrotpilot_comparison.angle_control: Current upstream includes ANGLE_CONTROL/LFA_ALT detection and LKAS_ANGLE_CMD plus an authority ceiling. This does not establish native angle-command support on this project vehicle (2022 Ioniq 5 HDA1); local output remains torque.

recovery.temporary_steering_fault: Temporary MDPS fault blocks latActive. The general SOFT_DISABLE state has a 3-second timer; disappearance of soft-disable conditions before expiry returns to enabled. Silent temporary steering events have different alert classification.
recovery.can_loss: canTimeout becomes canBusMissing, invalid CAN becomes canError. Both events are IMMEDIATE_DISABLE and NO_ENTRY. After disabled, state-machine engagement requires a new ENABLE event with NO_ENTRY absent; signal recovery alone is not the transition.
recovery.always_lateral_caveat: This fork has AlwaysLateral and independent lateral gates. Do not equate a global disabled state with every lateral-path condition; steerFaultTemporary/Permanent directly prohibit lateral activation.
recovery.panda_transport: Native pandad exits when a Panda disconnects; its Python wrapper loops and re-enumerates/reconnects and relaunches the native process. This does not confirm ECU recovery. Native sender discards messages older than one second.
recovery.startup_ecu_session: Hyundai init calls disable_ecu for configured longitudinal ownership. disable_ecu retries initial setup up to 10 times; periodic suppressed-response tester-present maintains the diagnostic session. This is not a continuous positive ECU response check.
recovery.steering_override: recovering_from_override and SteeringHandover recover steering authority after driver intervention, especially in the angle path; these are unrelated to reconnecting an unresponsive ECU.
recovery.ecu_restore_scope: No general in-motion ECU reset or stock-camera/radar restoration-and-rearm state machine was found in the inspected Hyundai runtime path. CarInterfaceBase.deinit is a stub and Hyundai does not override it in this snapshot.

temporary_steering_recovery.scope: Port the bounded temporary-fault ACTIVE return, not unrestricted recovery from CAN loss, Panda faults, or ECU hardware failure. No firmware change or safety-hook bypass.
temporary_steering_recovery.root_cause: VehicleStateParser previously marked fresh critical CAN invalid when the decoded MDPS assistance fault was nonzero, so SafetySupervisor treated a recoverable EPS assistance condition as immediate global FAULT and stock-ECU restoration.
temporary_steering_recovery.decoded_signal: Existing eps_fault decoding is preserved: MDPS 0xEA bit 54 length 2 (MDPS_LkaFailSta in the pinned DBC). This is a bounded assistance-fault recovery policy, not proof that every reported ECU fault is temporary.
temporary_steering_recovery.states: ACTIVE -> SOFT_DISABLING -> ACTIVE before a fixed 3-second deadline. At or after the deadline, FAULT remains latched even if the next received sample reports no EPS fault. Existing numeric states 0..4 are preserved; SOFT_DISABLING is 5.
temporary_steering_recovery.recovery_prerequisites: Existing arm and selected channels, fresh valid finite enabled command, fresh checksum-valid critical CAN, healthy Panda with correct mode/param/harness, cleared EPS assistance fault, and Panda controls_allowed. Never force Panda permission or retake ECU ownership during driving.
temporary_steering_recovery.paused_output: Zero torque and inactive LFA request, controller integral reset and target angle reset to the current measured angle. A separately allowed longitudinal command remains active with unchanged conversion/range behavior. Raw 0x12A LFA is blocked when lateral is not allowed.
temporary_steering_recovery.ownership: Retain the existing vehicle safety mode, channel selection, heartbeat and disabled-ECU tester-present sessions during the temporary window. Do not invoke enter_no_output_mode or stock restoration just for a temporary EPS pause.
temporary_steering_recovery.intervention_priority: Brake and ACC errors retain longitudinal latching; configured CANCEL and explicit disarm cancel the pause. CAN loss, Panda hardware/health faults, mode drift, rejected lateral frames, stale/invalid commands and recovery timeout keep the existing hard-fault path.
temporary_steering_recovery.initial_engagement: EPS assistance faults prevent initial takeover/engagement; no 3-second window starts from inactive ARMED state.
temporary_steering_recovery.telemetry: VehicleState.valid now describes fresh critical CAN reception independent of eps_fault. Existing ROS message fields and numeric state values are preserved. Diagnostics add eps_fault and soft_disable_remaining_ms and warn during SOFT_DISABLING.

adas_diagnostics.method: UDS 22 F1 00 and 22 F1 10 identification, and 19 02 FF DTC status in the existing/default ECU session.
adas_diagnostics.scope: ADAS-related physical-address candidates on existing ECAN only; HVAC is a transport reference.

interpretation.diagnostic_result: Seven ADAS-related candidate endpoints did not respond to either identification DID or DTC list. HVAC reference returned the same raw 923413/status 09 record. No ADAS DTCs were obtained; timeouts do not establish zero faults or ECU absence.

mdps_last_frame.scope: Latest captured broadcast state only, not stored MDPS DTCs. Warning/LKA fault flags are zero in this frame.

interpretation.capture_limit: Nonzero RX overflow means the capture is not loss-free. Missing frames are a dated observation on this route, not proof of failed/unpowered ECUs or all-network absence.
interpretation.endpoint_identity: Pinned upstream Ioniq 5 FW records use forward camera 0x7C4 and radar 0x7D0; upstream 0x730 is an ADAS Driving candidate on LKA steering platforms. The local implementation's 0x730 camera-ownership assumption remains unverified. Neither 0x7C4 nor 0x730 responded here; no runtime endpoint change made.
interpretation.next_diagnostic_focus: Establish ADAS reachability: inspect camera/radar power and harness/network connection, and compare with a Hyundai-capable OBD/GDS all-system read. Present evidence does not distinguish ECU power/wiring, architecture/diagnostic routing, or ECU faults.

adas_diagnostics.actions: Temporary ELM327 mode, power-save off, USB packet-tail reset, inactive Panda heartbeat, then restoration of original safety/param/power-save. Only identification/DTC/ISO-TP flow-control CAN writes. No ECU session change/reset, communication control, DTC clearing, actuator requests, firmware or heartbeat-policy change.
sources: Pinned opendbc hkg_can_fd_checksum and UdsClient; actual completed Panda USB/UDS query report

dtc_clear.authorization: User explicitly requested one DTC initialization/clear followed by checking recurrence.
dtc_clear.scope: One physical-address UDS 14 FF FF FF request per previously queried ADAS-related candidate and responding HVAC reference; no all-network scan.

interpretation.confirmed_clear_acknowledgement: HVAC 0x7B3 accepted service 14 with positive response 54. This acknowledges the request, not repair of the underlying fault.
interpretation.immediate_re_read: HVAC returned the same raw DTC 923413/status 09 (TEST_FAILED and CONFIRMED_DTC) immediately after the acknowledged clear. Cannot classify this as a resolved historical/transient fault; exact component/cause remains unconfirmed.
interpretation.adas_clear_status: Seven candidate addresses timed out on clear and before/after reads. Clearing success and code absence are unconfirmed; do not silently repeat clears.
interpretation.post_clear_limit: Some faults require their monitoring conditions or later operation cycles before recurrence; immediate code absence would not by itself prove repair.
